stories.title: Tech Stocks Slide as AI Spending Spooks Wall Street
stories.whats_going_on: The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 2.6% after Meta disclosed further heavy spending commitments on artificial intelligence. Meanwhile, Treasury yields posted their biggest drop since 2023 as investors sought safer assets.
stories.what_it_means: Markets are starting to question whether massive corporate spending on AI will deliver quick profits. This split the stock market, with tech slumping while broader segments of the market saw gains.
stories.why_care: If you hold broad market index funds or pensions exposed to big tech, high volatility can cause short-term swings in your overall portfolio balance.

stories.title: Oil Prices Jump to Five-Month High Amid Mideast Tensions
stories.whats_going_on: U.S. oil pushed above $100 a barrel and Brent crude hit a five-month high following heightened geopolitical tensions and warnings from Iran. President Trump accused Iran of attempting to manipulate the oil market.
stories.what_it_means: Higher crude oil prices directly feed into the cost of fuel, transport, and energy production globally. When oil spikes, it adds an upward pressure on everyday household bills.
stories.why_care: Costlier oil can eventually filter down to higher prices at the petrol pump and push up wider inflation figures, squeezing your monthly disposable income.

stories.title: French Borrowing Costs Flash Fresh Euro Zone Warning Signs
stories.whats_going_On: French borrowing costs surged as mounting national debt and political risks sparked investor concern. Analysts are watching closely to see if this debt stress could spread across the wider euro zone.
stories.what_it_means: When a major European government sees its borrowing costs rise, it often reflects broader nervousness about public finances in the bloc. Credit rating agencies are keeping a sharp eye on these developments.
stories.why_care: Turmoil in European government debt markets can indirectly influence regional borrowing conditions and broader investor sentiment across the continent.

stories.title: British Retail Sales Slip as Households Tighten Purse Strings
stories.whats_going_On: Retail sales in Great Britain fell as struggling households cut back on spending amid mounting economic pressures. This negative update comes just ahead of the upcoming national budget announcement.
stories.what_it_means: Consumers are feeling the pinch from the cost of living and shifting economic confidence, leading them to rein in discretionary purchases. Policymakers monitor these trends to gauge the underlying health of the high street.
stories.why_care: A slowdown in consumer spending is a classic sign of households protecting their cash buffers as everyday essentials eat further into monthly pay packets.
